title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
subtitle: Date sponge in a dark toffee sauce
excerpt: A soft, dense sponge loaded with pureed dates, drenched in a dark, buttery toffee sauce. Served warm with the sauce poured over and a jug more on the side.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sticky toffee pudding is one of Britain's most celebrated desserts, though its precise origin is disputed. The Sharrow Bay Hotel in the Lake District is often credited with popularising it in the 1970s, though similar recipes predate this. The defining technique is soaking chopped dates in boiling water with bicarbonate of soda before adding them to the batter: the alkali breaks down the dates into a soft, caramel-like paste that gives the sponge its dark colour and intense sweetness. The toffee sauce is made separately and poured over the warm pudding to serve, with more on the side.

recipeTools.notes: A 20 x 20 cm baking tin or 6 individual dariole moulds.

content.text: The dates must be soaked and slightly broken down before being added to the batter: do not skip this step. The sponge is done when a skewer comes out clean, but it will still feel soft and moist to the touch. Make the toffee sauce while the sponge bakes. Pour some sauce over the sponge as soon as it comes out of the oven and return to the oven for 5 minutes: this soaks the pudding through.
Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease and line a 20 x 20 cm tin. Put the dates in a bowl, add the bicarbonate of soda, then pour over 200 ml boiling water. Leave for 10 minutes.
Beat the 80 g butter and 150 g brown sugar together until light. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Add the vanilla. Fold in the flour.
Mash the dates roughly with a fork and fold into the batter with all their soaking liquid. Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Make the toffee sauce: melt the 100 g butter and 150 g brown sugar in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the cream and salt. Simmer for 3 minutes until thickened and glossy.
Pour half the sauce over the hot sponge. Return to the oven for 5 minutes. Serve in warm bowls with the remaining sauce poured over and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
